# `silk/machine/actor`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Actors: a machine that performs the effects its transitions queue.

A transition never does work. It queues effects as values, and an actor hands each one to a
performer, in the order they were queued. The performer is an effect function of the program,
so its requirement row names every service the machine's effects use. It can send events back
with [`Reply.send`](#Reply.impl.send), for example the result of a request.

[`Actors`](#Actors) keeps the snapshot in memory. [`Durable`](#Durable) has the same functions and saves the
snapshot after every change.

Import as `Actors` with `import silk.machine.actor { Actors }`.

Public declarations: 4.

<a id="Actors.impl.settle"></a>

### Associated function `settle`

```silk
pub effect fn settle<'env, S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X, F, ? R>(
    snapshot: &mut Snapshot<S, E, C, X>,
    perform: effect fn<'env>(X, &mut Reply<E>) -> () ! F ? R,
  ) -> ()
    ! F | OutOfMemoryError | TransitionLoopError
    ? R | &mut Allocator
```

Performs every queued effect and processes every event in the mailbox, until both are empty.

#### Details
Effects run one at a time, in the order they were queued, and before the next event of the
mailbox is processed. An effect leaves the snapshot before it is performed, so a failure of
the performer does not perform it a second time.

<a id="Actors.impl.serve"></a>

### Associated function `serve`

```silk
pub effect fn serve<'env, S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X, F, ? R>(
    snapshot: &mut Snapshot<S, E, C, X>,
    inbox: &Receiver<E>,
    perform: effect fn<'env>(X, &mut Reply<E>) -> () ! F ? R,
  ) -> ()
    ! F | OutOfMemoryError | TransitionLoopError
    ? R | &mut Allocator
```

Runs the actor on events from `inbox` until the machine finishes or the channel closes.

#### Details
The actor settles first, so effects left in a restored snapshot are performed before the
first event. Fork this effect as a fiber to run the actor beside other work.

#### Gotchas
It does not take delayed transitions. Use [`drive`](#Actors.impl.drive) for a machine that has them.

<a id="Actors.impl.drive"></a>

### Associated function `drive`

```silk
pub effect fn drive<'env, S: Machine<E, C, X>, E: 'static, C, X, F, ? R>(
    snapshot: &mut Snapshot<S, E, C, X>,
    sender: &Sender<Signal<E>>,
    inbox: &Receiver<Signal<E>>,
    perform: effect fn<'env>(X, &mut Reply<E>) -> () ! F ? R,
  ) -> ()
    ! F | OutOfMemoryError | TransitionLoopError | TaskIdExhaustedError
    ? R | &mut Allocator | &mut Scheduler | &mut SystemClock
```

Runs the actor with its timers until the machine finishes, a `Signal.Stop` arrives, or the
channel closes.

#### Details
The actor reads the wall clock from `SystemClock` before each signal and takes the delayed
transitions that are due. While it waits, a child fiber sleeps until the next deadline and
then sends `Signal.Tick` through `sender`, so a delayed transition is taken on time without
another event. `sender` must send to the channel of `inbox`.

#### Gotchas
The actor holds a `Sender`, so its channel does not close when the other senders are
dropped. Send `Signal.Stop` to end an actor whose machine has no final state.

<a id="Durable"></a>

## `Durable`

```silk
pub struct Durable
```

Actors that save their snapshot after every change, so a program that stops can start again
from the last save.

### When to use
Use `Durable` in place of [`Actors`](#Actors) for a machine that must survive a restart: a workflow, an
order, a session. Each function takes one more argument, `save`, an effect function that
stores the snapshot, for example as JSON in a file or a database row. To start again, decode
the stored snapshot and pass it to [`Durable.drive`](#Durable.impl.drive) or [`Durable.serve`](#Durable.impl.serve), which first perform
the effects that were still queued.

### Gotchas
An effect is performed at least one time, not exactly one time: when the program stops while
the performer runs, the effect is performed again after the restart. Make effects safe to
repeat. An event that was received and not yet saved is lost with the program.

<a id="Durable.impl.settle"></a>

### Associated function `settle`

```silk
pub effect fn settle<'env, S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X, F, G, ? R, ? Q>(
    snapshot: &mut Snapshot<S, E, C, X>,
    perform: effect fn<'env>(X, &mut Reply<E>) -> () ! F ? R,
    save: effect fn<'env>(&Snapshot<S, E, C, X>) -> () ! G ? Q,
  ) -> ()
    ! F | G | OutOfMemoryError | TransitionLoopError
    ? R | Q | &mut Allocator
```

Performs every queued effect and processes every event in the mailbox, until both are
empty, and saves the snapshot after each of them.

#### Details
`save` gets the snapshot after each event is processed, with the effects that step queued,
and again after each effect is performed, with the events the performer sent back. A
program that stops between two saves starts again from the last one: an effect that was
being performed is still queued there and is performed again.
